observation: Round 2 pushed the oblique Hough path to its in-bounds limits (threshold 20, maxLineGap 60) and the proxy moved only 0.5555 -> 0.5565 (correspondence_f1@15 0.1754 -> 0.1770); sam_fill_rate (0.779), ring_count_error (0) and depth_nan_ratio (0.114) were unchanged, K-row gate unchanged (10 propagated prompts at 241.7 px pitch, residual ~4 px). The round-2 detected_lines.png still shows only ~10 oblique segments, all on the two K edges (green +angle at y~1445-1480, red -angle at y~1620-1640) and only in the outer rings (x<600 and x>1800); the six middle rings (x~600-1800) yield no line at any setting because the outlier map there is dominated by bolt-pocket blobs, and the horizontal A1/B1 (~798) and B2/A3 (~2301) joints have no outlier signal at all (only bolt rows at ~730/850 and ~2240/2340, 50-60 px off the boundary, which would be counted as unexplained lines if admitted). Two unexplained red segments sit on bolt rows at y~1690-1700 (x~550 and ~1750), ~60 px below the K lower edge. Detection is therefore saturated: no in-bounds detecting knob can add supported joint lines without adding bolt-row false lines, and binary_threshold is dead in [100,127] on this map. Stages 1-3 remain healthy (residual 2.7 cm, orient_axis_corr 0.99997, retention 0.818, NaN family-normal and concentrated on fixtures: cable tray at the top, K-row bracket run at y~1500-1540, walkway/cable strips at the bottom). Stage 5 is template-locked with SAM masks at K 1469-1629 / B1 798-1462 / B2 1635-2298 / A1 129-797 / A3 2301-2968 and scores 0.76-0.97; measured geometry differs from the template only slightly: ring pitch 241.7 px = 1208 mm vs segment_width 1200 mm, detected K-edge slopes ~+5..+8 deg (upper) and ~7 deg (lower) vs taper angle 6.12 deg, K-edge pair spacing ~164 px = 820 mm vs K_height 823.8 mm (aligned, keep).
rule: Experiences 7 (tuning order): detection has been validated and exhausted (line count consistent with ring count, gate residual single-digit px), so the remaining lever is stage-5 SAM geometry, which is only worth touching once stages 1-4 are settled - that is now the case. Experiences 9: trust the between-round proxy delta and corroborate with artifacts; round 2's delta was small but non-negative with all lean features stable, so the round-2 detecting set is locked in rather than reverted. Ontology d8/r_fix_height_priors and r_fix_template: align pixel-domain template priors (segment width, taper angle) with the geometry actually measured on the map; precondition satisfied (resolution unchanged at 0.005 m/px). Experiences 3/10 anti-patterns: do not chase NaN cosmetics via theta tightening or curvature smoothing when NaN is family-normal and sits on fixtures.
failure_mode: Residual stage_4_detection.f_missing_lines is now irreducible within bounds (A/B joints absent from the outlier map; K edges recoverable only in outer rings) with a guard against f_spurious_lines from bolt rows. The remaining addressable item is a minor stage_5_segmentation.f_template_mismatch: template segment_width and taper angle sit slightly off the measured ring pitch (1208 mm) and K-edge slopes (~7 deg), so per-ring template masks are ~1.7 px narrower than the ring and the K wedge edges diverge from the detected line slopes by up to ~2 px at the ring margins.
rationale: Lock the round-2 detecting set (binary 110, oblique 20, horizontal 45, vertical 2000, gap 60, tolerance 12, snap on) so the exact 10/10 ring count, bolt-row guards and best-so-far line yield are preserved, and use the final round for the minimal SAM geometry alignment that round 2 deferred: set sam.segment_width to 1208 mm so each ring template spans the measured 241.7 px pitch instead of 240 px (closing the ~1.7 px inter-ring template gap that leaves thin unlabelled seams between adjacent ring masks and slightly under-covers the ring margins), and set sam.angle to 7.0 deg so the K wedge template edges follow the measured +/-7 deg oblique K-edge lines rather than the 6.12 deg prior, bringing the SAM-derived K boundaries closer to the detected lines at the ring margins where the 15 px correspondence test is tightest. K_height stays at anchor (823.8 mm) because the measured K-edge spacing (~164 px = 820 mm) already matches within ~1 px. Denoising and enhancing stay at anchor: theta tightening would remove partial A1/A3 lining for a cosmetic NaN gain and shift the K-row design position, and raising curvature_threshold risks joint over-smoothing that would erode the few supported K-edge lines. Expected effect: sam_fill_rate up slightly (seam closure), correspondence_f1@15 flat to slightly up (K boundaries better co-linear with detected lines), ring_count_error 0 and depth_nan_ratio unchanged; if the SAM change is neutral, the round-2 detecting configuration remains the best candidate for selection.
